anchor.title: Dia nacional de Timor-Leste
anchor.text: Timor-Leste assinala o seu dia nacional a 20 de maio, aniversário da restauração da sua independência em 2002, após o domínio português e a ocupação indonésia.

meanwhile.title: Ainu recognized as indigenous
meanwhile.text: Japan's Diet formally recognizes the Ainu as an indigenous people of Hokkaidō, acknowledging a long history of dispossession. Language revival, museums and a cultural resurgence follow across the island.

meanwhile.title: Mayotte becomes a French department
meanwhile.text: Following a 2009 referendum, Mayotte becomes France's 101st department in 2011. Comoros continues to claim the island, while migration from the other Comorian islands toward Mayotte has created a dangerous sea crossing and a persistent political dispute.

meanwhile.title: A nation mourns its founder
meanwhile.text: Félix Houphouët-Boigny, who led the country from independence, dies after decades in office, closing a defining era. His death opens a period of contested succession in Ivorian politics.

meanwhile.title: Genghis comes back
meanwhile.text: The new constitution drops the word socialist, and the man whose name had been unmentionable for seventy years is put on the money, the airport, the vodka, and a forty-meter steel horse.

meanwhile.title: Mount Fuji
meanwhile.text: UNESCO lists Mount Fuji as a cultural World Heritage Site, honoring its hold on Japanese art and faith. From Shizuoka the listing embraces the Sengen shrines, the pilgrim trails and the pine grove of Miho where Fuji frames the bay.

meanwhile.title: Bengaluru
meanwhile.text: The state formally restores the Kannada name, along with eleven other cities. As in Mumbai and Kolkata, usage lags the gazette, and what the city is called turns out to be a question about who it is for.
